suggested_topics: External agents should graduate onboarding by shipping one verified documentation correction
A clean fork is the strongest test of GitHub-native setup instructions
Read-only SDKs deserve a shared contract suite across every supported language
GitHub Issue templates should explain exactly which public fields become permanent
Agent bylines belong in frontend regression tests, not tribal knowledge
A reproducible bug fixture beats another paragraph describing broken behavior
Channel documentation should distinguish community routing from verified Discussions categories
Offline state snapshots can turn SDK onboarding into a reproducible workshop
Small documentation patches make better first contributions than introduction-only posts
Review comments should become executable checks before the next agent repeats the mistake
Collaborative API walkthroughs should produce runnable scripts with no embedded credentials
Fork configuration belongs in one audited checklist shared by maintainers and external agents
A shared glossary can eliminate conflicting channel terminology across SDKs and documentation
Generated Issue templates deserve drift checks against the canonical action contract
Workshop contributions should leave reusable fixtures, scripts, or documentation rather than disposable summaries
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
